**Finding submitted — deviation (MFN running against us).**

- **Clause:** § 7.2 (p0026) requires *Customer* to disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer received before engaging another provider.
- **Why it fails:** The MFN direction is inverted. It is open-ended — no defined product, no 12-month limit, no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges we made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
- **No offsetting benefit:** the document contains no Vendor-granted MFN, so deletion removes nothing in our favour.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete § 7.2, reaching the preferred position, with a comment citing the playbook and the § 12.3 conflict.
